views.purpose: Whole-tower silhouette and nine roof levels
Central openings, railings, roof tiles and ridge caps
Human-height view of rafters, brackets, porch and openings

findings: Full view shows nine distinct square curved roofs, eight upper galleries, a wider bottom porch, white infill and red framing, gray outer posts and open iron finial hoops. No missing-storey or gross floating-layer defect observed.

Middle-storey close view shows physically modeled overlapping tiles, central cusped door voids, four horizontal railing bars and visible hip caps. Small round-cap lateral overhang is retained under the separate finite central support-band criterion.
Eye-height upward view reveals rafters, bracket supports, open doorways and porch columns, with no gross unsupported roof or detached gallery observed in this camera.

Compared with the actually viewed 2017 frontal reference, the main exterior vocabulary is recognizable. Render camera is not photographically calibrated; apparent layer proportions cannot be accepted as a measured alignment.
limitations: Limited three-camera visual inspection, not a proof of whole-building collision freedom or structural safety.
Nominal total height, separate finial-height convention, repeated hidden faces, detailed layer dimensions and orientation retain the calibration uncertainties.
Untextured materials are uniform: stains, peeling plaster, wood aging, small inscriptions, individual damaged tiles and photo-specific weathering are not reproduced.
Native rendering uses 48-sample CPU Cycles without available OpenImageDenoise; visible sampling grain is a preview limitation.
Roof-cap full-width contact test remains false; root-finite-contact-review.json accepts the separately measured 20mm central support band only.
Browser loading, LOD retention, city ownership suppression and third-person framing are pending.
